text:
Claire: FYI scheduling a short maintenance window in eu-west1 WED 02:00-03:30 UTC. Goal: GPU driver bump + fan sensor firmware sync. We'll cordon racks in 15m cohorts and do rolling reboots, aim for no more than 3 racks simultaneously out of service.
Hao: Which racks/pools are in the cohort? any tenants pinned to those?
Claire: Cohorts: racks a1-a6 (pool-eu-1), b1-b4 (pool-eu-burst). Tenants pinned: none high-priority, but Dedicated customers on pool-eu-1 will be routed to eu-backup. I'll post the exact mapping.
Priya: Can we avoid preheating KV cache on these racks? it's expensive on token budget.
Claire: We'll do targeted kv preseed only for canaries (2 nodes) to keep regen latency bounded. Rest will be cold; Optimize suggests this is fine for this window.
Miguel: ETA for each rack? also what's the fallback if a driver upgrade fails?
Claire: ~12-18m per rack including drain and uncordon. Fallback: rollback driver package, power-cycle GPU, and put nodes back in pool. If rollback fails we'll fail traffic to backup pools and open incident.
Noah: ops-bot, can you schedule the drain jobs and post runbook link?
ops-bot: Scheduled: 2026-03-25T02:00:00Z -> 2026-03-25T03:30:00Z. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/egpu-fan-sync. Notifying oncall.
Priya: Any cost impact for rerouting to backup pools? we might cross a reserved threshold.
Claire: Expected short bump ~3-6% for that hour; committed capacity should cover most traffic but we may spill to burst; finance flagged potential ~$120 extra for the window.
Hao: Please paste the drain/uncordon commands so SRE oncall can follow.
Claire: Command snippet: ```
# cordon + drain with graceful 2m pod-termination
kubectl cordon node-01
kubectl drain node-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=600s
# after firmware and driver update
kubectl uncordon node-01
```
Lina: Do we need to coordinate with networking for egress throttle adjustments? last time we saw transient queueing.
Miguel: yes, open egress throttle to +20% for the window and add a short ramp-down 10m after completion.
Claire: I'll add egress change to the comms. Also enabling auto-fallback policy for the API route: prefer eu-backup then us backup.
Priya: Any customers I should notify ahead of time? dedicated & enterprise only?
Claire: Send heads-up to Dedicated accounts and those with pinned eu-west workloads. I'll draft the notice.
Hao: Oncall names for the night?
Noah: Oncall: Miguel -> Lina -> Hao. Incident channel: #incidents. Pager escalation set.
Lina: If we see KV regen > 600ms p50 on canaries, abort and rollback.
Claire: Agreed. Adding these thresholds to the runbook.
Miguel: One more ask — telemetry: tag all uptime/latency diffs with maintenance_id=eu-fan-sync-8001234567 for postmortem.
ops-bot: Telemetry tag added to scheduled job metadata.
Claire: Final checklist: 1) Post customer comm 24h and 2h before. 2) ops-bot schedule + runbook link. 3) Network throttle + rollback plan. 4) KV preseed limited to canaries. 5) Cost estimate shared with finance. 6) Oncall rotation set.
Priya: OK, I'll approve the customer comm copy.
Hao: I'll be on standby for driver rollback.
Noah: I'll monitor capacity dashboards and post updates in thread during the window.
Claire: Thanks team — ping here as cohorts start. :thumbsup:
